# CSS and SCSS in Quarto

CSS controls the appearance of a website. It can change colors, fonts, spacing, borders, layout, and responsive behavior.

SCSS is an extension of CSS. It allows the author to use variables and other features that make a stylesheet easier to maintain.

## How this website uses SCSS

The `_quarto.yml` file applies `styles.scss` to the entire website:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme:
      - cosmo
      - styles.scss
```

The stylesheet uses variables for reusable design decisions:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/

$primary: #0f766e;
$body-bg: #fffdf8;
$body-color: #243b53;
```

## Styling a class

The following SCSS creates a reusable card style:

```scss
/*-- scss:rules --*/

.simple-card {
  background: #ffffff;
  border: 1px solid #d9e2ec;
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 1rem;
}
```

The class can then be used in a QMD file:

```markdown
::: {.simple-card}
### A simple card

This content receives the reusable style.
:::
```

::: {.simple-card}
### Example styled card

This card uses the `.simple-card` class from `styles.scss`.
:::

## Why styling is useful

- It creates a consistent appearance across pages.
- It makes headings and sections easier to scan.
- It helps important links and notes stand out.
- It allows the layout to work on different screen sizes.
- It separates content from presentation.

## SCSS layer boundaries

The comments below are required by newer versions of Quarto when an SCSS file is used as a theme layer:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
/* variables go here */

/*-- scss:rules --*/
/* style rules go here */
```
